paragraphs.text: Hi, my name is Hana. I will be showing you my album. Before I start, however, let me introduce my family members to you. There are five in my family.

First is me. I am ten years old. I go to Toto Elementary School, and I am in grade three. I love to draw pictures, sing and dance. I can swim well and would like to learn taekwondo someday. My favorite food is barbecue chicken, spaghetti and chocolate ice cream.
Second is my dad. He is forty years old and is really tall. He loves me the best, then my brothers. He is kind and often reads books to us. He loves to hike on the mountains with us on the weekends.

Third is my mom. She is 35 years old and is a bit short. But I think my mom is the prettiest. She is an English teacher and can speak English really well. Although she is strict, she can be fun to be with.

Next is my brother Bada. He is seven years old and is in kindergarten. He is very playful and hot-tempered. He is never interested in school work or food. My mom is worried that he doesn't eat enough.
Finally, my baby brother Hada. He is one and has a double chin. But he is so cute. He smiles a lot when I sing and dance for him.

I have two grandmothers and one great grandmother. My great grandmother is one hundred years old. She is very old but she knows the names of all my family and greets us when we go visit her. My grandmother on my father's side is 74 years old and she lives with my great grandmother. She is very kind and does whatever I ask her. My grandmother on my mother's side is 73 years old. She lives in a house and has two dogs. She loves dogs.
These are my family members, and you will get to see them in my album. I hope you have fun. See you!
As always, my mom will come in a few minutes.
Mom: Wake up! It's time to get up.
Hana: But I'm sleepy. I'm so tired.
Mom: It's already 7:30. I told you to go to bed earlier.
Hana: Okay, okay, I'm getting up now!
Mom: Put your pajamas away, and don't forget to make your bed. I'll be in the kitchen. Wake Bada up please.
Hana: Bada, put your pajamas away and make your bed too.
Bada: Why do I always have to make my bed?
Hana: You know we need to keep our rooms neat.
Bada: You are not my mother, and this is my room! I can do whatever I want!
Hana: I'm telling Mom. Mom!
So the day began, with my busy morning.
The morning was dark, without a bit of sunshine. It was rather chilly too.
Hana: Bada, don't forget your umbrella.
Bada: My umbrella? Why?
Hana: It might rain today.
Bada: How do you know?
Hana: The weather forecast said so last night.
Bada: I don't see any raindrops. Do you want to bet?
Mom: Your sister is right. Take your umbrella, just in case.
Hana: I told you! My brother never listens to me. See you, Mom!
Mom: See you later. Both of you have a good day!
We made a bet to see whether or not it would rain. Can you guess who won? The loser had to take out the garbage that night.
I wish my mom could always be waiting for me when I get home from school.
Hana: I'm home, Mom. Where are you?
Mom: I'm in the kitchen. You're home early.
Hana: The teacher let us out early today.
Mom: That's right. It was your first day. How was your class?
Hana: It was fun.
Mom: Did you make many new friends?
Hana: Oh yes. A girl named Susan sits by me.
Mom: Susan? Invite her over sometime. By the way, what's your teacher's name?
Hana: Hmm. I forgot. I'll find out tomorrow.
I am not very good with names. But I did remember my partner Susan's name.
My mom always tells us to eat good food. We are not allowed to buy any junk food.
Hana: When are we eating, Mom?
Mom: As soon as your brother comes home.
Hana: What are we having today?
Mom: Spaghetti.
Hana: Yum, that's my favorite!
Bada: I'm home, Mom.
Mom: Hi, Bada. Go wash your hands please. Lunch is almost ready.
Bada: I'm not hungry. Can I go out and play?
Mom: No, come and eat right now. Your sister is waiting.
Bada: Can I play after lunch then?
Mom: Sure you can.
My brother is not interested in food. He is only interested in toys and his friends.
My brother Bada is not as healthy as he seems.
Mom: Bada, you have a runny nose.
Bada: I do?
Mom: Here is a tissue. Blow your nose.
Bada: Oh, Mom!
Mom: What's wrong?
Bada: My nose is bleeding!
Mom: Come over here and let me see. Keep your head down.
Bada: Will it stop?
Mom: It will stop soon. Don't worry. Here, drink this milk.
Bada: Mom, it's too hot.
Mom: No, it's just warm. Drink it all. How do you feel?
Bada: Ahh, I feel much better.
Mom: You should drink more milk every day, Bada.
Bada: I know, I know.
Mom: Go to the bathroom and take a shower now.
Bada: Yes, ma'am!
He doesn't look sick to me. I am sure he was picking his nose. That's why it was bleeding. Bada, stop picking your nose!
At times, I get a fever and a sore throat. However, after a good night's sleep, I feel much better.
Mom: Are you feeling okay?
Hana: I feel sick, Mom.
Mom: Oh no. You have a fever. Let me check your temperature. You do have a fever. It's 37.8°C. I will get you some medicine. Here you go. Take one pill at a time.
Hana: Can I lie down?
Mom: Sure. You'd better go to bed early.
Hana: But, Mom, I didn't brush my teeth yet.
Mom: Well then, get up and go brush them now. Don't forget to floss.
Hana: Okay.
No matter how sick or tired we may be, we should always brush our teeth.
!@It's a warm and sunny Sunday afternoon. My mom does her work when Dad is home.
Dad: Honey, Hada has the hiccups.
Mom: I am busy right now. Could you get him some water?
Dad: Where is it? Is it in the fridge?
Mom: No, it's on the table. Make sure you warm it just a bit.
Dad: Hey, it stopped. Good for you, Hada!
Mom: Give him some water anyway. He might be thirsty.
Dad: Yes, Mom! Let's get you some water!
!@ My dad usually helps my mom. I wonder if all fathers are like that. Hmm.
Mommy and Daddy take turns reading books to us. It was Daddy's turn tonight.
Dad: Did you choose the book?
Bada: Yes. I would like this book tonight.
Dad: Okay. Let's read this storybook. Do you know what it's about?
Bada: I'm not sure. Something about a snail?
Dad: That's right. It's about a snail with a big house.
Bada: Hmm. That sounds interesting.
Dad: Your sister loved this book.
Bada: Come on, Dad. Please read it to me.
Dad: Here we go.
Bada is usually wild and active. However, when it comes to reading, he becomes such a good boy.
We are happy to choose the books ourselves. That way, we can read our favorites over and over.
Dad : The end.
Bada: That was a fun story.
Dad: I am glad you liked it.
Bada: Could you read it one more time, please?
Dad: I'm afraid it is too late. I will read it to you tomorrow night.
Bada: Well then, can I just look at the pictures again?
Dad: All right. Don't stay up too long.
Bada: Yes, Dad. Good night.
Dad: Sleep tight.
As you can see, Bada can't read yet. He is already seven years old! I learned to read and write when I was six years old. Oh well. What can you do?
When my mom is busy, I help her out. Of course, I am the big sister.
Hana: Mom, Hada is crying.
Mom: Could you check his diaper?
Hana: Oh! Can I change it?
Mom: Sure, go ahead.
Hana: Bada, get me a fresh diaper!
Bada: Can't you see I'm busy right now?
Mom: Come on, Bada. Your sister cannot leave the baby alone.
Bada: Here you go.
Hana: Hada, say thank you to your big brother. Let me change your diaper. Be a good boy now.
Hada is such a cute baby. He is different from Bada. He smiles and laughs a lot. He listens well when I read a book to him. I am sure he will grow up to be a good boy.
I love to play with Hada. Whenever I go near him, he turns his head to look at me. How does he know that I am there?
Hana: Mom, look at Hada.
Mom: Is something wrong?
Hana: Hada is smiling at me. Maybe he is happy because I changed his diaper.
Mom: I guess so.
Hana: You like your big sister, don't you, Hada? Yes, you do. Come on. Smile back at me again. There you go. Good boy!
Mom: Hana, it's time for bed.
Hana: Okay, Mom. I have to go to bed now. See you tomorrow, Hada. Good night.
Hada must know that I am his big sister. He always smiles when I talk to him. Mom says that babies can smell well. Can they smell like dogs? I wonder . . .
I don't have a single cavity. Do you want to see? Ahhh. But my brother Bada already has two cavities.
Bada: I am all finished, Mom.
Mom: Are you really?
Bada: Yes!
Mom: Let me see. Say, ahhh. Bada, did you brush your back teeth?
Bada: I brushed the front teeth.
Mom: Come on, go back to the bathroom. Let me brush your teeth. Here is the toothpaste. Don't squeeze too hard. Let's get your back teeth. Brush up and down. Now, you try.
Bada: Up and down, up and down.
Mom: There you go. Now, take some water and gargle.
Bada: Okay, am I done now?
Mom: Let's see. Looks good to me. Next time, don't forget to brush your back teeth, okay?
Bada: Yes, ma'am.
Come on, Bada, keep brushing up and down, up and down!
We have two bathrooms, but sometimes they are both full.
Mom: What's wrong? Why are you squirming, Bada?
Bada: I, I have to go to the bathroom.
Mom: Well, go quickly then.
Bada: I can't. Dad is still in there.
Mom: What about the other one?
Bada: Hana is taking a shower.
Mom: Come on. Hold it just a little longer. Honey, can you hurry? Bada has to use the bathroom.
Dad: Okay. I am almost done. Oh, we're out of toilet paper.
Mom: I'll get another roll.
Bada: Oooh, I can't hold it anymore.
Bada learned a lesson. Don't wait until the last minute. When you want to go pee, don't wait. Go quickly!
Bada is very untidy. Just look at his room and you'll know what I mean.
Mom: Oh my goodness! There's water everywhere. Hana, Bada, come over here.
Hana: Mom, what's wrong?
Bada: Yeah, Mom. I'm here.
Mom: Who spilled the water here?
Hana: Not me!
Bada: Uh . . .
Mom: Bada, were you playing with water?
Bada: Uh, I was not playing. Actually I was going to water the plants.
Mom: I see. But look! The floor is slippery. Someone could get hurt.
Bada: Sorry, Mom. I will wipe it up.
Mom: Thank you, dear. Here is a mop.
Bada: Hana, will you help me?
Hana: Are you kidding? No way!
Sorry, Bada. Mopping is your job!
I had been waiting for my birthday. I was born in the summer.
Hana: All right! My birthday falls on a Saturday this year!
Bada: Your birthday? When is it?
Hana: On July 13. I am going to have a great birthday party!
Bada: What about my birthday? When is it?
Hana: It's in the winter. Go and ask Mom about it.
Bada: Mom!
Mom: Yes, dear.
Bada: When is my birthday?
Mom: Your birthday is on December 29.
Bada: Is that soon?
Mom: No, dear. It is still months away.
Bada: How long is that?
Mom: Hmm. You have to wait about 180 days.
Bada: 180 days? Wow!
Hana: Mom, can I invite some friends to my birthday party?
Mom: Sure. Just let me know how many will be coming.
Hana: Thanks, Mom!
July is my favorite month because it is the month in which I was born. When were you born?
I wanted to design a special invitation card. So I used the computer.
Hana: I am going to make a nice invitation card.
Bada: An invitation card? Can I watch?
Hana: Sure, but just be quiet.
Bada: Okay.
Hana: Done! Let's print it out! Hmm. Looks good to me. Let me show it to Mom.
Bada: Can I see it too?
Hana: Mom, Mom. Here is my invitation.
Mom: What does it say?
Hana: This is what I wrote.
What: Hana's Birthday Party
When: Saturday, July 13 at 2 p.m.
Where: At my house (phone: 348-8079)
Game: A treasure hunt, finders keepers!
Hana: How is that?
Mom: Sounds like fun.
Bada: What's a treasure hunt?
Mom: You look for hidden things.
Bada: What kind of things?
Hana: Wait and see.
How do you plan your birthday party? I like to have a special event every time.
It is one day until my birthday. The invitation cards have been sent. Mom will prepare the food.
Hana: Mom, tomorrow is the big day.
Mom: I know. What would you like for your birthday meal?
Hana: My favorites! Barbecued chicken, spaghetti, and kimbab , please.
Mom: What about a cake?
Hana: Oh, yeah. A cake too.
Bada: I want a yummy ice cream cake.
Hana: It's not your birthday, Bada. Mom, I would like a chocolate cake please.
Mom: Sure. How many do you expect?
Hana: Hmm, about 9 to 11 people.
Mom: I see. Well, let's go grocery shopping then.
Bada: Are you going to buy the cake now?
Mom: I will do that tomorrow.
Hana: Let's go, Hada!
We put up many pretty balloons in the living room. That night I dreamed a wonderful dream.
It was my birthday! Many of my friends came over.
Everyone: Happy birthday to you.
Happy birthday to you.
Happy birthday, dear Hana.
Happy birthday, dear Hana.
Hana: Thank you for coming to my party! Thank you for the gifts! Please, help yourselves!
Friend 1: Hana, when are we going to do the activity?
Friend 2: You mean the treasure hunt?
Friend 3: Yeah, what's that about?
Hana: I have hidden 15 treasures in the house. Finders keepers!
Friend 4: All right! I can't wait!
All of my friends found at least one treasure each.
Mom helped Bada find one too. We had a great time!
My friends loved the treasure hunt. Bada was screaming with joy when he found a treasure. Why don't you try it on your birthday?
Friend 1: Hana, I had a good time.
Friend 2: Yeah! The treasure hunt was great.
Hana: I am glad you guys liked it.
Everyone: Thank you, Mrs. Kang!
Mom: Thank you, everyone, for coming.
Everyone: Bye, Hana.
Hana: Bye! See you on Monday. Whew, the party was fun and the food was great. Thanks, Mom.
Mom: You are very welcome.
Bada : Hana, look what I found!
Hana: Good for you, Bada. You can keep it.
Bada: All right! Hana, can we do the treasure hunt again?
Hana: If you behave and do what I say.
Bada: I can do that.
Hana: Then, we will do it again tomorrow. For now, you must help Mom clear the table.
Bada: Yes, Ma'am!
Bada behaved and did what I told him. The next day, we did the treasure hunt again. It was really fun!
Have you ever heard of a treasure hunt? We did a treasure hunt on my birthday. My friends loved it. Bada was crazy about it.
Bada: Hana, could we do the treasure hunt again? Please? Please?
Hana: I am busy right now. I have to finish my homework.
Bada: Can we do it after you are done? I will grant you three wishes.
Hana: All right. Hmm. First, I wish you to clean up the living room.
Bada: Okay! Done! I cleaned the living room. How's that?
Hana: Hmm. Pretty good! Second, I wish to drink a glass of milk.
Bada: Right away! Here you go.
Hana: Good job. And last, I wish you to massage Mom's shoulders.
Bada: No problem! Mom!
Mom: Bada . . . Ha, ha, ha . . .
Bada: Is that enough?
Hana: That's enough. Now, let's do the treasure hunt.
Bada: Hurray! Hurray!
I got three wishes everytime Bada wanted to do the treasure hunt. He is my brother and I like him.
I felt sorry for Bada. Why? Because I made him do all the work. Remember the three wishes?
Hana: I will hide a treasure. Close your eyes.
Bada: Okay. I closed my eyes.
Hana: Hey, don't peek!
Bada: I'm not! Tell me when to open my eyes!
Hana: Now, you can open your eyes. There is a hidden treasure in the house. Where could it be?
Bada: Give me the first clue.
Hana: Look on the place where you sleep.
Bada: Where I sleep? Aha! Here it is! Mom, what does it say?
Mom: It says, "Go brush your teeth."
Bada: Of course, the bathroom! Brush my teeth. Here it is!
Bada ran around the house looking for the treasure. And at last, he found it. Boy, was he happy!
Healthy body, healthy mind! Do you exercise every day? No? Not even once a week?
Hana: What are you doing, Mom?
Mom: I am exercising. Do you want to exercise with me?
Hana: Sure, I'd love to.
Mom: Let me turn on the music. Let's do some stretching. Here we go.
One, two, three. Stretch your arms out. Left, right, left, right.
Hana: Left, right, left, right.
Mom: Now bend your knees.
Hana: One, two, one, two.
Mom: Stretch your leg out like this.
Hana: Like this? Oh, that hurts!
Mom: Stand up. Turn your head around.
Hana: One, two, three.
Mom: Now breathe in and out slowly.
Good job, Hana.
Hana: That was fun, Mom. Let's work out every morning!
Mom: Sounds good to me!
Yes, I began to exercise every morning. Look, I'm starting to get muscles now!
It was a beautiful Sunday afternoon. After lunch we wondered what we should do. Dad had a good idea.
Dad: Do you guys want to play dodge ball?
Bada: What is dodge ball?
Hana: You throw the ball and try to hit someone. They dodge the ball.
Bada: That sounds like fun. Let's play, Dad!
Dad: Let's go outside and play then. Wait. We need one more person.
Hana: Mom, are you busy? Let's play dodge ball.
Mom: I will be right out with Hada. You go ahead.
Bada: Let's go! Let's go!
Dad: Put on your sneakers. Hana, can you get the ball?
Hana: Yes, Dad.
Bada: I'll take it.
Hana: Hey, be careful!
Bada: Sorry.
Dad: Wait for me!
My Dad is fun to be with. He teaches us new games to play, and I like them.
Summer is a wonderful season to play. It can be hot, but fun.
Dad: Let's divide into two teams. Where's Mom?
Mom: I am here.
Hana: Let's do rock, paper, scissors.
Everyone: Rock, paper, scissors!
Bada: Dad! We are a team!
Hana: All right! I am with Mom.
Dad: When you get hit, you are out of the game.
Bada: Can I catch the ball?
Dad: Yes, you can. When you catch the ball, it is your team's turn. Remember not to throw it in anyone's face.
Hana: Here it goes! Darn!
Bada: It's my turn now. Ha-ya ! I got you, Hana!
Mom: No, Hana dodged the ball. Here it goes!
Bada: Dad, look out!
We had so much fun! Sorry, Hada! You can play with us when you're a little bigger.
Next weekend is my Grandma's birthday party. I get to play with my cousins all day!
Bada: Dad! Dad! Why is there a big circle around that number on the calendar? What is it?
Dad: Let me see. Oh, that's Grandma's birthday. This year it falls on a Saturday.
Hana: We will go to see Grandma?
Dad: Of course! Do you like going to Grandma's?
Bada: Sure! I get to see Grandma and play with my cousins. It's great!
Hana: I love to wear my party dress. But it may be too small for me now. Let me ask Mom.
Bada: How will we get there? Last time we took the train.
Dad: We will drive.
Bada: But, I want to ride a train, Dad.
Dad: Sorry, Bada. This year we could not buy any tickets.
Bada: Why not?
Dad: They were all sold out.
Bada: Oh boy!
Bada and I are excited. We love our Grandma. She is so kind and generous.
Mom and Dad were busy getting ready for the trip.
Hana: What are you doing, Mom?
Mom: I'm wrapping some gifts.
Hana: Who are they for?
Mom: They are for Grandma.
Hana: Can I help you?
Mom: Sure, you can. Bring me the ribbon.
Hana: Here you go.
Mom: Thanks. By the way, have you tried on your party dress?
Hana: I did. It still fits me well. Should I put it on?
Mom: Yes. I would like to see it just in case.
Hana: How do I look?
Mom: Oh, you look so wonderful. Take it off now, and save it for the party.
Hana: What about Bada and Hada?
Mom: I have to buy a new suit for Bada. Hada can wear Bada's old one.
Do you have fancy party clothes? I love the color of mine. I can't wait to see Bada and Hada wearing their suits.
It was a long ride to Grandma's house. There was heavy traffic on the road.
Bada: Are we there yet?
Dad: We are almost there. Hold on just a little longer.
Bada: Mom, I'm thirsty. I need a drink.
Mom: Hana, can you get him a drink? It's in the cooler.
Hana: Okay. Here you go, Bada.
Dad: Hey, everyone. Grandma is over there waiting for us.
Bada: Really? Where? Where?
Mom: Look on your right. There!
Hana: Grandma! Grandma!
Bada & Hana: Grandma!
Grandma: Oh my goodness. My babies! Is that Hada? Oh, he has grown so much. Let's go in. Everyone is waiting.
Bada: Already? All right!
We were so happy to see Grandma and our cousins. What a wonderful time with the family!
Bada is beginning to learn phone manners. Let's see how he is doing.
Mom: Bada, could you answer the phone?
Bada: Sure. Hello?
Mom: Say, "This is the Kangs' residence."
Bada: This is the Kangs' residence. Who? Oh, she's not home yet. Bye.
Mom: Who was that?
Bada: I don't know. A girl asked for Hana.
Mom: Next time, say, "Who is calling please?"
Bada: Okay, Mom. "This is the Kangs' residence. Who is calling please?" How was that?
Mom: Well done, Bada.
Bada: Hada, repeat after me. "This is the Kangs' residence. Who is calling?" Boy, you need to practice. Here you go. I am going to Tom's house. See you later, everyone.
Mom: Be back by five.
Bada: Yes, Mom.
Bada did a good job on the phone. I guess he is growing up.

30.title: Mrs. Kim Is on the Phone

paragraphs.text: Every time Bada answered the phone, he remembered what Mom had told him to say.
Bada: Hello. This is the Kangs' residence.
Mrs. Kim: Hi, Bada. Is Mom home?
Bada: Who is calling please?
Mrs. Kim: Oh, this is Mrs. Kim.
Bada: Hi, Mrs. Kim. I will get her for you. Mom! Mom! Where are you?
Mom: I am in the bathroom, Bada.
Bada: Mrs. Kim is on the phone.
Mom: Tell her that I will call right back.
Bada: Okay. Hello, Mrs. Kim? Mom is in the bathroom. She said she will call you back.
Mrs. Kim: Very well. Thank you, Bada.
Bada: You're welcome, Mrs. Kim. Bye.
Everyone says that Bada has such wonderful phone manners. Even I am surprised!
I used to do all the work before. But now I can ask Bada to do it for me.
Mom: I will be gone for a while. If someone calls, say, "Can I take a message?" Here is a pen and paper.
Bada & Hana: Yes, Mom.
Hana: Bada, I have to finish my homework. You answer the phone, okay?
Bada: Sure. Don't worry. I can do that. Hello, this is the Kangs' residence.
Mr. Kim: Is your Dad home?
Bada: My dad? Nope, he is not home yet. Can I take a message?
Mr. Kim: That's fine. I will call back.
Bada: Wait! Mom said that I have to take a message.
Mr. Kim: All right, then. This is Mr. Kim. My number is 378-8907. Please ask him to call me.
Bada: Mr. Kim. 378-8907. Is that right?
Mr. Kim: That's right. Bye.
Bada: Thank you. Bye.
Bada always knows how to get exactly what he wants.

32.title: I Have a Message for You

paragraphs.text: When Dad comes home, we all line up and greet him.He simply loves that.
Bada: Hi, Dad.
Hana: Hello, Daddy.
Mom: Hi, honey. How was work?
Dad: Hi, everyone. I've been busy today.
Bada: Dad, I have a message for you. Here you go.
Dad: Let me see. Hmm. Who is this? M K?
Bada: That's Mr. Kim and his phone number.
Dad: I see. Thank you, Bada. You did a good job.
Bada: Really? From now on, I will take all the messages.
Hana: Wow, Bada. Can you spell?
Bada: I know my ABCs. That's enough.
Mom: He's right.
We all had to laugh at Bada. It looks like nothing can stop him now!
Mom brought something home. Do you want to know what it was?
Mom: Hana and Bada! Look what I have.
Bada: What’s up, Mom? What is it?
Mom: It is a scale. It shows you how much you weigh.
Bada: How much do I weigh?
Mom: Hold still. Let me see. Bada weighs 22 kilograms.
Bada: Is that heavy?
Mom: It’s about right. But you need to eat more. Now it’s Hana’s turn.
Hana: I will do that later.
Bada: Oh, come on, Hana. I want to see how much you weigh.
Hana: All right. I will do it then.
Bada: How much do you weigh?
Mom: Hana weighs 28 kilograms.
Bada: Wow! Hana, you weigh so much.
Hana: No, I don’t!
I don’t think I’m heavy. What do you think? How much do you weigh?
It was Hada’s turn to get weighed. We never leave him out. He seems to have grown so much.
Bada: Mom, what about Hada?
Mom: Yes. I need to know his weight.
Bada: I’ll get him. Oh, he is heavy, Mom.
Mom: Put him on the scale. Oh, no. He needs to be still. I know what. Let me hold him and we’ll get weighed together.
Hana: Then you can get weighed alone.
Mom: That’s right. Let’s see. Come here, Hada. We weigh 61.5 kilograms. Now Hada can sit down. I will check my weight. I weigh 52 kilograms. So how much does Hada weigh?
Hana: Hada weighs 9.5 kilograms.
Mom: That is correct.
Hada weighs quite a lot. He grows so fast.
Hear the Christmas carols. See the twinkling lights. It’s the Christmas season!
Hana: Mom, Christmas is just around the corner.
Mom: Yes, dear.
Bada: I can’t wait for Santa to come. He will give me a nice present.
Dad: What do you wish to get?
Bada: Well, this year, since I have been such a good boy . . . I wished for a nice pair of rollerblades.
Dad: Hmm. Really? I see . . .
Bada: What about you, Hana? What did you ask for?
Hana: I asked for a mini camera. I like to take pictures.
Dad: Boy, Santa will need to work very hard this year.
Hana: Done! Bada, quick! Turn off the light!
Bada: Okay, here we go.
Everyone: Wow! It’s beautiful!
Santa Claus brings happiness to us all!
It was a bright Christmas morning.
Bada: Is it morning yet? My present! Hana, get up! It’s Christmas morning!
Hana: Huh? Oh, yes!
Bada: Where is my gift? Here it is! Wow, it’s heavy.
Hana: Here is mine too.
Bada: Wow, how cool! Dad, look!
These roller blades are exactly what I wanted! All right!
Hana: This camera is perfect. Thank you, Santa!
Bada: Mom, may I try the roller blades right now?
Mom: You can go out after you eat breakfast, Bada.
Bada: Boy, I am hungry. Mom, please fix me some breakfast quickly!
What a sweet day. Merry Christmas, everyone!
Mom has big news. Do you want to hear about it?
Dad: Mom has some news for you guys.
Mom: Do you remember Aunt Sunny?
Bada: Who is that?
Hana: Oh, I remember her, Mom. She is your best friend. She came to Korea last year.
Mom: That’s right. But call her Aunt Sunny. She is like a sister to me. We were invited to her wedding!
Hana: That means we are going to America?
Mom: Except for Dad. He has to work.
Hana: Sorry, Dad. But don’t worry. I will take lots of pictures and bring them back to you.
Dad: Thank you, dear.
Bada: What about Hada, Mom?
Mom: Grandma will take care of him.
Hana: How long are we staying?
Mom: We will stay for about a month.
Yes, a trip to America! I will tell you all about it. Wait and see!
I guess I am not dreaming. I am at the airport!
Hana: Okay, Bada. Strike a pose and I will take a picture.
Bada: Sure. How is this?
Hana: Good. Say, "Cheese!" One, two, three!
Mom: We are all set to go. You’d better say good-bye to Dad now.
Hana: So soon? Oh, Dad. I will miss you.
Bada: Me too. I will call you every day, Dad.
Dad: Oh, I will miss you guys too. Call me when you get there.
Mom: We will, honey. Please take care of Hada.
Dad: Don’t worry about him. Hana and Bada, listen to your mom and behave yourselves. Have a safe trip.
Hana & Bada: Bye, Dad. See you later. We will miss you.
Bada: Mom, I miss Dad already.
Mom: We will see him soon, Bada.
Who can stop us now? Here we go!

39.title: I Was Flying Above the Clouds!

paragraphs.text: Can you imagine? I was flying above the clouds!
Bada: This is boring. I thought flying would be fun.
Mom: It’s almost dinnertime. Here is the menu. We can have either salmon or chicken. Choose one.
Hana: Hmm. I want chicken.
Bada: What is salmon?
Hana: It’s a kind of fish.
Bada: Yuck! I hate fish. I will have chicken.
Flight attendant: Salmon or chicken?
Mom: Salmon, please.
Hana: Chicken, please.
Bada: Me too. Chicken, please.
Flight attendant: Anything to drink?
Mom: Yes, I will have some water.
Hana: Do you have milk?
Flight attendant: Sure, we do. Here you go.
Hana: Thank you.
Bada: Mom, can I have a Coke?
Mom: Sorry, Bada. No Coke.
Bada: Okay. Milk, please.
It was a long flight. But I didn’t mind. I will have so much fun soon.
Hooray! We have finally arrived.
Mom: Let’s line up.
Bada: What now, Mom?
Mom: We show our passports to the man. He will ask some questions. That’s all.
Immigration: Good afternoon! Your passports, please.Where are you from?
Hana: We are from Korea!
Immigration: How long do you plan to stay?
Mom: We will stay for a month.
Hana: My Aunt Sunny is getting married!
Immigration: How wonderful! Welcome to the United States. Enjoy your stay here.
Mom: Thank you.
Bada: THANK YOU!
Mom: Now, we have to pick up our bags.
Mom: Hmm. Excuse me, sir. Where is the baggage claim area?
Officer: Go straight ahead and turn right.
Mom: Thank you.
Officer: My pleasure, ma’am.
I can’t wait to go out and see the city!
Aunt Sunny and her fiancé were waiting for us. Hello, there!
Mom: Sunny!
Sunny: Oh, Young-Hee. How have you been? I am so glad you could come.
Hana & Bada: Hello, Aunt Sunny.
Sunny: Oh, my! Hana and Bada! Welcome, welcome! Let me introduce you to my fiancé. His name is Tom Blake. Tom, this is my best friend, Young-Hee.
Tom: How do you do? Call me Tom.
Mom: Nice to meet you, Tom. You can call me Young. These are my children, Hana and Bada.
Tom: Beautiful names. Hello, Hana. Hello, Bada.
Hana & Bada: Hi. Hello.
Sunny: Come on. Let’s go home. You guys must be tired.
Tom: Here. Let me take your bags.
Mom: Thank you.
Tom: Let’s go to the parking lot.
Bada couldn’t take his eyes off the car.
It was our first evening in San Francisco.
Sunny: This is Chinatown.
Hana: Look at the stores and the buildings. I can hear them speak Chinese.
Bada: Oh no. I can’t speak Chinese.
Tom: Don’t worry, Bada. They speak English too.
Bada: Whew!
Tom: Let’s go in.
Waiter: Good evening, ladies and gentleman.
Sunny: A table for five, please.
Waiter: Right this way, please.
Hana: Ni-hao-ma.
Waiter: Ho.
Tom: I didn’t know you spoke Chinese!
Hana: Just the greeting. That’s all.
Waiter: Here is the menu. Let me know when you are ready.
Mom: Thank you.
I love Chinese food. One day, I would like to visit China!
I couldn’t wait to eat. I was so hungry!
Waiter: Would you like anything else?
Sunny: Just a minute, please. Hana and Bada, do you want anything else?
Bada: I want the sweet thing with beef.
Sunny: What is that?
Hana: He means sweet and sour beef.
Sunny: Oh, I see. Would you like that too, Hana?
Hana: I don’t mind, Aunt Sunny. I am hungry.
Sunny: Okay, okay. A dish of sweet and sour beef, please.
Waiter: Yes, ma’am. Would you like anything to drink?
Sunny: Some cold water, please.
Hana: May I have cold water too?
Waiter: Sure.
Tom: I would like a glass of house wine, please.
Waiter: Yes, sir.
Bada: Mom, may I have a Coke, please?
Mom: Alright, Bada. Just this one time.
Bada: Yes! I would like a Coke, please.
Waiter: Right away!
Bada loves soft drinks. They're not good for your teeth, you know!
My Aunt Sunny’s wedding is coming up. She must be very excited!
Mom: Look! This is Union Square.
Hana: Wow, this place is huge. Look at all the people and the stores. Are you getting something for Dad?
Mom: No, not for him. It’s for Aunt Sunny. We are having a bridal shower tomorrow.
Hana: A bridal shower? What is that?
Mom: The bridal shower is a party. We prepare many gifts for the bride.
Hana: That’s interesting. What are you going to buy, Mom?
Mom: I’m going to buy her a tablecloth. There. Let’s look at the store directory. Home interior . . . Ah, here it is. H24. Are you hungry?
Bada: No, Mom.
Hana: I’m hungry, Mom.
Mom: We’ll eat after we shop. Is that Okay?
Hana: Sounds good.
I saw beautiful things to decorate the house with. Wow!
Yes! The store was full of beautiful things.
Clerk: Can I help you?
Mom: Yes, please. I am looking for a tablecloth.
Clerk: This way, please. All the tablecloths are in that corner. Let me know if you need help.
Mom: I see. Thank you. Excuse me. Do you have this in gold?
Clerk: Oh, yes. Here you go.
Mom: That’s perfect. Thank you.
Clerk: You’re welcome.
Mom: I would like to buy these two, please.
Clerk: Sure. Cash or credit card?
Mom: Credit card, please.
Clerk: One moment, please. Sign right here, please.
Mom: Okay. There.
Clerk: Thank you. Here is your card and the receipt.
Mom: Thanks.
What a wonderful tablecloth! It has gold lace all around it.
After shopping, we were very hungry, so we went to eat lunch.
Mom: Hana, you can order whatever you want. Here is the money.
Hana: What about Bada?
Mom: I will order for both of us.
Hana: Let me try.
Clerk: May I help you?
Hana: Yes. I would like a cheeseburger and a small order of French fries, please.
Clerk: Anything to drink?
Hana: A small orange juice, please.
Clerk: For here or to go?
Hana: For here.
Clerk: That’ll be $4.25, please.
Hana: Here you are.
Clerk: A five dollar bill. That’s 75 cents change. Thank you.
Hana: Umm . . . Can I have more ketchup?
Clerk: Here you are.
Hana: And where can I get a straw?
Clerk: The straws are on the counter to your left.
Hana: Oh, I see them. Thank you.
Clerk: You are very welcome. Next, please.
Yes, I ordered all by myself! I did a good job!
Tomorrow, I’m going to a garage sale. Do you know what a garage sale is? Why don’t you come with me?
Hana: What are we doing tomorrow?
Sunny: We’re going to a garage sale.
Bada: What’s that?
Mom: Let’s find out.
Sunny: At garage sales, people sell things they don’t need or want anymore.
Mom: How much is this?
Woman: Oh, that’s fifty cents.
Hana: What’s that?
Woman: That’s a record player. Listen.
Hana & Bada: Wow! What are these?
Woman: These are cookie cutters. You can make cookies in these shapes.
Hana: How much are they?
Woman: Ten cents each.
Bada: I like this!
Woman: It used to be my son’s. You can have it for free!
Bada: Thank you very much!
Woman : You’re welcome!
Bada: Look what she gave me!
Hana: Look what I got!
Mom: Oh, you can make cookies now.
In America, people don’t just throw away things. Other people may want them. Instead, they have garage sales. Garage sales are lots of fun!
I love reading books!
Tom: This is our public library.
Hana: So many books!
Tom: Do you like to read?
Hana & Bada: Yes!
Tom: What kind of books do you like?
Hana: I like fairy tales.
Bada: I like COMIC BOOKS!
Librarian: SHH! Please be quiet!
Bada: Oh, sorry!
Tom: We have to be quiet in the library.
Bada: Can I . . . ? Oops! Can I read here?
Hana: Can I look around by myself?
Tom: Sure, but come back here, okay?
Hana: Okay! I love fairy tales. And I love mysteries. Oh, and I really love animal stories. I am interested in science too. Tom, how many books can I borrow?
Tom: Only five books, Hana. After you finish them, we can come back.
Hana: Oh! Thank you!
Librarian: Do you have a library card?
Tom: Yes, here you go.
Librarian: You must return these books by next week.
Hana & Bada: Bye!
I can’t wait to go back to the library next week.
Aunt Sunny and Tom are very busy. So we’re going to see a movie.
Mom: What movie do you want to see?
Hana: The Unicorn Princess.
Mom: How about The Adventures of Max the Wonder Dog ?
Hana & Bada: Okay!
Mom: One adult and two children, please.
Hana: We’re going to see The Adventures of Max the Wonder Dog.
Clerk: Okay. Enjoy the show!
Mom: Thank you. Do you want some popcorn?
Hana & Bada: Yes!
Bada: Can I have some juice too?
Hana: Nothing for me, thanks. Mommy, where do we sit?
Mom: You can sit wherever you like.
Bada: Really?
Mom: See? There are no seat numbers.
Hana: Bada, can you pass me the popcorn? Mommy! Bada won’t give me the popcorn.
Mom: Bada!
Voice-over : Meet Max! The wonder dog!
Bada: The movie’s starting, Hana!
Hana: I know! Give me the popcorn!
It was a great movie! Have you seen any good movies lately?
Going to the park is lots of fun. There is so much to do!
Hana: Can I help you?
Mom: Can you take the paper cups over there?
Hana: Are we going on a picnic?
Sunny: Yes, we’re going to Golden Gate Park.
Tom: What do you want to do first?
Bada: Can we rollerblade?
Sunny: Sure! Let’s go rent some skates!
Hana: Watch this!
Bada: Mom! Can you take a picture of us, please?
Mom: Okay, everyone, say, "Cheese!"
Hana, Bada, Tom & Sunny: CHEESE!
Tom: Let’s go for a boat ride.
Bada: I can see fish!
Mom: Hold still, Hana. I’m going to take a picture.
Hana: Oh, the bird flew away!
Mom: What’s over there?
Tom: That’s Queen Wilhelmina’s Garden and Windmill.
Mom: It’s beautiful.
Hana: Look at the tulips, Mom!
Sunny: Excuse me, can you take a picture of us, please?
Man: No problem! Okay, everybody, say, "Cheese!"
Everyone: CHEESE!
We took many photographs at the park. Do you want to see my favorite one?

51.title: A Postcard for Dad and Hada

paragraphs.text: I miss Dad and Hada. I wonder how they’re doing?
Sunny: Do you need anything, Hana?
Hana: Yes, I’d like to buy some postcards for Daddy and Hada.
Sunny: What a good idea! Let’s look in this shop.
Hana: Here is a nice one. It shows the Golden Gate Bridge.
Sunny: That’s beautiful!
Hana: I’ll take these.
Hana: Dear Daddy and Hada , How are you?
I miss you very much. We are having lots of fun in America.
Mom: Do you want some cookies, Hana?
Tom: Hey, Hana! What did you do today?
Hana: I wrote a postcard to my daddy and Hada. Can you take me to the post office?
Tom: Sure thing. Let’s go.
Clerk: Hello. What can I do for you today?
Hana: I want to send this postcard to Korea.
Clerk: Korea? Okay, that’ll be 75 cents.
Hana: Here you go.
Mom: Did you send the postcard, Hana?
Hana: Yes. I hope Daddy likes it. When will he get it?
Tom: Probably in a week or so.
Since Dad can’t come to San Francisco, I sent San Francisco to him!
Aunt Sunny asked me to be her flower girl. I get to wear a pretty dress and hold a basket full of roses.
Sunny: Today we’re going to the dressmaker’s.
Mom: You will get your flower girl dress, Hana.
Sunny: What’s your favorite color?
Hana: I like pink.
Seamstress: Now it’s your turn.
Mom: You’re going to love your dress.
Hana: Oh, it’s my favorite color!
Seamstress: Try it on!
Mom: Are you ready, Hana?
Seamstress: Oh, you look like an angel!
Mom: Hana, you look so beautiful!
Seamstress: Don’t forget the flowers in your hair. What’s your favorite flower, Hana?
Hana: My favorite flower is the rose.
Mom: Then your basket will be filled with red roses.
Sunny: Okay, I’m ready to come out! What do you think?
Mom: You are the most beautiful bride ever!
Hana: Aunt Sunny, you look so pretty! Boy, now I’m hungry!
Sunny: What’s your favorite food, Hana?
Hana: I love barbecued chicken, spaghetti, and, of course, chocolate ice cream!
Mom: Hana, I think you’ve had too much to eat.
Hana: But I’m still hungry, Mommy.
Sunny: Let her enjoy her ice cream, Young-hee.
Mom: I just hope you don’t get sick!
Aunt Sunny looked so beautiful in her wedding dress. My dress is very pretty too. I can’t wait for the wedding day!
Ooh! I think Mom was right. I ate too much!
Mom: What’s wrong, Hana?
Hana: I’m not feeling well, Mommy.
Mom: Where do you feel sick?
Hana: My stomach hurts.
Mom: I thought you ate too much yesterday.
Hana: I know, Mommy. I’m sorry.
Sunny: There you are, Young-hee. Bada isn’t feeling well.
Mom: Neither is Hana.
Sunny: How are you feeling?
Hana: I have a stomachache. How is Bada?
Sunny: He has a runny nose and a cough.
Hana: Poor Bada! I hope he’s better soon.
Sunny: I’d better go to the drugstore. l’ll get some medicine for you and Bada.
Hana: Thank you.
Mom: My poor baby.
Sunny: Here, take this. Ahh . . .
Hana: Yuck! It tastes awful!
Sunny: You have to take this three times a day.
Hana: I wish I wasn’t sick.
Sunny: Hey, Bada! How are you feeling?
Bada: I’m hungry!
Sunny: How about some chocolate ice cream?
Hana: Not for me!
Bada and I are feeling much better now. I’ll never eat so much ice cream again!
Aunt Sunny’s family is coming for the wedding. We got to meet them.
Sunny: Mom! Dad! It’s so good to see you!
Mother: Sunny! How are you? You look beautiful!
Father: You look wonderful, dear!
Sunny: Let me introduce you to my best friend, Young-Hee.
Mom: Hello. It’s nice to meet you.
Father: And what’s your name?
Hana: My name is Hana. Nice to meet you.
Bada: And I’m Bada.
Sunny: This is my sister, Sherry.
Sherry: I’ve heard so much about you.
Mother: Where are you from?
Hana: We’re from Korea. How many brothers and sisters does Aunt Sunny have?
Mom: She has one sister and one brother.
Hana: Where is her brother?
Mom: He is living in France.
Father: How old are you, Bada?
Hana: He’s seven years old. And I’m ten.
Mother: So, Hana, I heard you are going to be the flower girl.
Hana: Yes. I have a beautiful pink dress.
Bada: I want to be a flower girl too!
Father: You can’t! It’s for girls only!
Sherry: The big day is coming up, Sunny.
Sunny: I know! It’s so exciting.
Hana: I can’t wait for your wedding, Aunt Sunny.
Mom: It’s going to be a beautiful wedding.
Aunt Sunny’s family is so nice!
It’s finally the big day! Today, Aunt Sunny and Tom are getting married!
Sunny: Oh, where are my hairpins?
Mom: I’ll look for them, Sunny.
Sunny: And my bouquet! Where is it?
Mother: It’s right here, dear.
Guest: Congratulations, Tom.
Tom: Thank you. Where are the rings?
Father: They’re in your pocket. Relax, Tom.
Mom: Are you nervous?
Sunny: I’m very nervous.
Hana: You look beautiful.
Sunny: Thank you for everything.
Father: It’s time.
Mom: Are you ready, Hana?
Hana: Yes, but I’m nervous too.
Mom: Don’t worry. You look beautiful, Hana!
Sherry: Oh, Hana looks like an angel!
Mother: She’s so pretty!
Guest 1: Look at the bride! She’s so beautiful!
Guest 2: What a beautiful bride!
Tom: . . . I do.
Minister: And do you, Sunny, take Tom as your loving husband?
Sunny: I do.
Minister: I now pronounce you husband and wife.
Bada: Congratulations, Aunt Sunny! Congratulations, Uncle Tom!
Tom: Thank you, Bada!
Mom: What a beautiful wedding!
Hana: Thank you for inviting us!
I am happy for Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom. They are going to Hawaii for their honeymoon.
While Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom were on their honeymoon, we decided to clean the house for them.
Hana: What are you doing, Mommy?
Mom: I want to wash these for Sunny.
Hana: How are you going to wash them all?
Mom: I’m taking them to the Laundromat. Do you want to come along?
Hana: This is my first time at a Laundromat.
Mom: Well, we need to find an empty washing machine.
Hana: Here, Mommy!
Mom: Can you change these into coins?
Hana: Can you change these into coins, please?
Woman: Here you go.
Hana: Thank you.
Mom: We’ll wash the blankets first.
Hana: They’re so heavy!
Mom: Yes, they are. Now, push the door and turn the dial. Then we sit here and wait!
Hana: What’s that?
Mom: That means the washing is finished. Help me put it into the dryer, Hana.
Hana: Now, what do we do?
Mom: Do you want some soda?
Hana: What is Bada doing?
Mom: He is helping Sunny’s parents clean the house.
Hana: They feel so soft and dry!
Mom: Thanks for helping me, Hana.
Mother: We finished cleaning the house.
Bada: I helped too, Mommy!
Mom: I’m so proud of you, Bada. And you too, Hana.
Mother: Your children are such hard workers!
Aunt Sunny’s house looks so clean! I can’t wait for her and Uncle Tom to come home!
Guess what! We’re going to Disneyland! But first, we have to buy a few things.
Mom: Kids, would you like to go to Disneyland?
Hana & Bada: Disneyland! Yeah! Yeah!
Mom: But first, we have to get some things.
Bada: When are we going to Disneyland, Mom?
Mom: We leave early tomorrow morning.
Hana: How are we getting there?
Mom: We’re driving. We need some sugar. Where is it?
Bada: Is this it, Mom?
Mom: No, Bada. That’s flour.
Hana: I’ll go and ask. Excuse me, where is the sugar?
Clerk: Sugar? Follow me. Here you go.
Hana: Thank you. Oh! Where is everybody? Cereals and pasta? No, I don’t see them. Drinks and snacks? Oh, where can they be? Mom? Bada? I think I’m lost.
Clerk: What’s your name?
Hana: Hana.
Clerk: Paging Hana’s mother! Please come to the checkout counter. Hana is waiting for you.
Mom: Hana! Hana!
Clerk: I’m glad you found your mom, Hana.
Hana: I was scared that I lost you!
Mom: Hana, don’t worry. You’ll never lose me!
Whew! That was a close call. I thought I would never see my mom again! I’m glad that clerk was so nice to help me.
We left early for Disneyland. It was a long drive!
Bada: How long will it take, Mom?
Mom: Oh, about six hours.
Hana: Six hours? That’s a long time!
Mom: California is a very big state.
Bada: I’m bored!
Mom: Let’s play a game! Do you know I Spy?
Hana & Bada: Yes.
Mom: Let me start. Umm . . . I spy with my little eye something that begins with C.
Hana: Is it carpet?
Bada: Is it coffee?
Mom: Yes! Bada, it’s your turn.
Bada: I spy with my little eye, something that begins with . . . umm . . . A.
Hana: Are we lost, Mom?
Mom: I hope not, Hana.
Bada: Mom! A man is coming.
Man: Can I help you?
Mom: We’re driving to Disneyland. Which way do we go?
Man: Turn right at the light. Then get on the highway. Keep going straight and you will reach Anaheim.
Mom: Thank you very much! Look, kids! We’re in Anaheim! We’re almost at Disneyland now.
Bada: Look at that car, Mom!
Hana: Maybe he’s a movie star! We’re here! We’re at Disneyland! Oh, I can’t wait to go on the rides!
Bada: Will I meet Mickey Mouse?
Mom: Of course! And Goofy and Donald Duck too!
The drive was very long, but it was worth it. Disneyland is like a dream!
There is so much to see and do at Disneyland. Have you been to Disneyland?
Mom: Which ride do you want to go on first?
Hana: The roller coaster!
Bada: No, I want to go on the balloon ride!
Mom: We can do both!
Bada: We’re up so high!
Hana: I feel like I’m flying.
Mom: Sit down, Hana!
Bada: They look like ants.
Mom: What do you want to ride next?
Hana: Can we ride the bumper cars?
Bada: But I want to see Mickey Mouse!
Mom: I’m sure we’ll see him soon, Bada.
Bada: Bam! I got you, Mommy!
Hana: Bam! Look out, Bada! I’m following you!
Mom: Oh . . . Hana! Here I come!
Hana: Mommy! Let’s get Bada!
Mom: Let’s have some cotton candy.
Bada: Yummy! This tastes good.
Hana: Oh, it’s so hot!
Mom: I know a great way to cool down!
Hana: Look at the fireworks!
Bada: My ears hurt.
Hana: The show’s about to begin.
Mom: Look, Bada! It’s Mickey Mouse!
Disneyland is not only fun for children, but it’s also fun for adults. I want to go again!
We were so tired from the wedding, so we went to the zoo to get some fresh air.
Mom: Now, stay close and listen to me.
Hana & Bada: Okay, Mommy.
Bada: Let’s see the tigers!
Mom: Come back here, kids!
Bada: Look at the tigers! They’re so big!
Mom: Don’t lean against the cage!
Hana: Come here, kitty.
Mom: Don’t put your hand in the cage!
Hana: Look at the elephants!
Mom: Don’t feed the animals!
Hana: Oh, sorry.
Bada: Do you want some peanuts instead, Mommy? Look at the monkeys! They’re so funny!
Hana: I want to touch them!
Mom: Don’t touch the monkeys! Oh, my hat! Give that back to me! Don’t you want to eat anything?
Hana: Whenever we do something, you always say "DON’T."
Bada: Yeah, so we don’t want to do anything.
Mom: I’m sorry. From now on, I’ll say "DO." Did you have a good time?
Hana & Bada: Yes, Mommy.
Mom: I’m sorry I was so mean.
Hana: We love you!
Mommy was so tired, but she still took us to the zoo. We had a good time with her.
Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom are back from their honeymoon. They took us on a cable car ride across San Francisco. We had so much fun!
Hana: Can we ride a cable car?
Sunny: Yes, here comes one now!
Mom: How much is the fare?
Tom: Don’t worry. It’s on us.
Hana: Wow! San Francisco is so beautiful!
Sunny: Yes, it is. Look! That’s City Hall.
Bada: Where? I can’t see.
Tom: Be careful, Bada. Hang on tight!
Sunny: This is our stop.
Tom: This place is called Fisherman’s Wharf.
Hana: What is that sound?
Sunny: That must be the sea lions.
Hana: Look! Look at all those sea lions!
Mom: Oh my! There must be at least a hundred of them.
Bada: Wow! I never saw a sea lion before!
Tom: We have to get back on the cable car again.
Hana: What’s that man doing?
Tom: He is turning the cable car around so that it can go in the opposite direction.
Sunny: He’s called a gripman.
Gripman: Does anyone want to help me?
Hana & Bada: Me! Me!
Gripman: Okay, now, Push! Push! Thanks for your help! All aboard!
Mom: Did you have a good time today?
Hana: Yes. It was a lot of fun.
Mom: I’m glad. And what about you, Bada?
Sunny: Looks like someone is ready for bed.
Bada was so excited to ride the cable car and see many other things. He was very happy but also very tired. So am I.
Wow! Time sure does fly! This is our last day in the U.S.A.
Sunny: I wish you could stay longer, Young-hee.
Mom: Me too, but my husband and Hada need me.
Bada: Can I stay here, Mom?
Sunny: Yes, you can live with us!
Hana: My suitcase won’t close, Mom!
Mom: I think you have too many things, Hana.
Hana: That’s from the zoo. That’s from Tom!
Tom: Did you enjoy your trip to the U.S.A.?
Hana: We had a great time!
Tom: How about you, Bada?
Bada: I’m going to live with Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom.
Tom: It was so nice to meet you. Come back and visit soon.
Hana: I hope you can come to visit Korea.
Tom: I hope so. Time flies by so quickly.
Mom: It feels like we just came yesterday.
Bada: Why do we have to go so soon?
Mom: Don’t you miss Daddy and Hada?
Sunny: I’m going to miss you!
Mom: Come and visit us in Korea.
Tom: We will.
Sunny: Oh, Young-hee, thank you for everything.
Hana: Good-bye, Aunt Sunny. Good-bye, Uncle Tom!
Bada: Good-bye!
Sunny & Tom: Good-bye! Take care!
It was hard to say good-bye to Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom. But we were looking forward to seeing Daddy and Hada.
Dad and Hada were at the airport to pick us up. It was wonderful to see them.
Dad: Hana! Bada! Over here!
Hana & Bada: Daddy!
Dad: Welcome home!
Mom: It’s good to be home.
Bada: We’re home!
Hana: Oh, how I missed you!
Mom: Take your suitcases into your rooms, kids.
Dad: I’ll help you. What was your favorite part of the trip?
Bada: Going to Disneyland!
Hana: I liked the cable car ride.
Mom: For me, it was the wedding.
Dad: Did you like San Francisco?
Bada: Yes! I want to go back!
Hana: But we missed you and Hada!
Dad: Next time we can all go together. Thank you, Hana. I love it!
Mom: This is for Hada.
Hana: I loved going to San Francisco. But this is my home sweet home!
Bada: I can’t sleep, Hana.
Hana: Me neither.
Mom: We must all have jet lag.
Hana: Jet lag? What’s that?
Mom: Right now it is afternoon in San Francisco. So our bodies still think we're in the U.S.
Bada: Will we have jet lag forever?
Mom: No. In a few days everything will be back to normal.
Hana: I’m glad we’re back home, Mom.
I have many wonderful memories of San Francisco. Where can I go next time? Do you have any places you’d like to visit?
That's my brother Bada. He is sad today. He misses our grandmother's dog, King.
Bada: Mommy, I want Grandma to come over to our house. Can I call her?
Mom: Okay, but let me dial.
Bada: Hello? Grandma, it’s me.
Grandma: Hi, Sweetie, how are you?
Bada: I’m fine. Grandma, can I talk to King?
Grandma: Sure.
Bada: King! Hey King! I miss you. King, when are you coming to see me? I hope to see you next week, okay?
Grandma: King looks very happy. What were you two talking about?
Bada: I want King to visit me next week.
Grandma: Sure, we’ll visit you next week.
Mom: Bada, what are you doing?
Bada: I’m waiting for Grandma and King.
Mom: They won’t be here until lunchtime. Why don’t you help me make lunch?
Bada: Okay. They’re here! Hello, Grandma! Hello, King. I have a present for you. Look, this toy puppy looks just like you.
Grandma: I think King’s scared.
Bada: See, King, it’s just a toy. King, sit! Good boy! Here’s a treat for you. King, down! Very good, King. Let’s try one more. King, roll over! What a smart boy, King!
Grandma: Well, it’s time to go.
Bada: Oh, don’t go. Can’t you stay a little longer?
Grandma: No, I have an important appointment tomorrow. I have to leave now.
Bada: Okay. Bye, Grandma. Bye, King.
Mom: It was nice seeing Grandma and King.
Bada: Yes, I miss King already.
My brother Bada loves animals. He loves King best.

65.title: A Special Day for Mother and Father

paragraphs.text: In May, we have Parents' Day. On this day, we thank our mother and father for everything they do for us. Bada and I are planning a surprise.
Hana: May 8 is Parents' Day, Bada.
Bada: What's that?
Hana: It’s a special day for Mom and Dad. Let's give them a big surprise!
Bada: What are you doing?
Hana: I'm making a card for Mom and Dad.
Bada: Can I make one too?
Hana: Of course. Here you go.
Bada: Why did you buy the flowers?
Hana: On Parents' Day we give Mom and Dad red carnations.
Bada: Why?
Hana: Red carnations mean that we love them very much.Bada, on Parents' Day we are going to surprise Mom and Dad. Okay?
Bada: Okay.
Hana: So don't say anything. It's a secret.
Dad: Hey, guys! What are you doing here?
Hana: Oh, hi, Dad!
Dad: Come on, let's go home.
Bada: It's a nice day. Let's walk, Hana. We'll see you at home, Dad!
Dad: Okay. See you! Hana and Bada are acting strangely.
Mom: It seems they are hiding a secret.
Dad: What kind of secret?
Mom: I don't know.
Hana: I think we should cook Mom and Dad dinner tomorrow night.
Bada: But I don't know how to cook.
Hana: Let's see . . . What do they like?
Bada: They like peanut butter and jelly sandwiches.
Hana: Oh, Bada, that's what you like. Let's make spaghetti!
Bada: Mom! Can you help me?
Mom: Later, Bada. I have to cook dinner now.
Bada: Help me, please.
Hana: Now, I need to make the pasta. Where does Mom keep the saucepan?
Dad: Hi, Hana. Where's your Mom? What are you doing?
Hana: Dad! You're not supposed to be here! You'll find out soon. Please!
Dad: Okay, okay.
Mom: Can I open my eyes now?
Hana & Bada: Yes. Happy Parents' Day!
Dad: What a nice surprise!
Bada: Thank you, Mom and Dad. We love you!
Bada and I were so happy to surprise Mom and Dad. We are so grateful to have them as our parents. What will you do for your parents on that special day?
Do you like flowers? What is your favorite flower? I like tulips. We went to the flower festival last week. It was beautiful!
Bada: Can we go on the merry-go-round?
Mom: Not today, Bada. Today, we are going to see the flowers.
Hana: Come on, Bada! Let's go look at the tulips!
Bada: But I want to go on the merry-go-round.
Hana: Oh, take a picture of me in front of the tulips, please.
Mom: Where is Bada? Bada? Bada?
Dad: Did you know there are over 30,000 flowers here?
Mom: Honey, let's find Bada first.
Dad: Oh, right. Sorry. Bada! Bada! He can't be too far away. Bada! Bada!
Hana: Wait! I think I know where he is.
Mom: Bada! Bad boy! You made us worry.
Bada: I’m sorry. But I wanted to see the merry-go-round.
Hana: Bada, we can go on the rides later.
Bada: Promise?
Hana: Promise. Now let's go see more flowers.
Bada: I’m sorry, Mom and Dad!
After that, even Bada enjoyed the flowers. Of course we went back to the park to ride the merry-go-round. So everyone was happy.
Summer vacation is just around the corner! This year we are going to the beach!
Mom: Are we ready to go? Do we have everything?
Dad: Yes, I think so. Okay, everyone! Hop in!
Bada: Can I have ice cream at the beach?
Mom: Of course you can, Bada.
Hana: I want to take a boat ride.
Dad: We can do that too. It's going to be so much fun at the beach.
Hana: Oh! And I want to build a sand castle!
Bada: Me too, Hana!
Hana: Oh, Mom! It's so beautiful! Can we go swimming now? Please? Please?
Mom: No, it's too late. But tomorrow we can go early in the morning. Okay?
Hana & Bada: YEAH!
Bada: Wake up! Hana! Mom! Dad!
Hana: What time is it? Why is it so dark? Oh no! It's raining!
Bada: We can't go to the beach!
Dad: Don't worry. We'll think of something.
Mom: Come on, you two. It's fun!
Hana: No, thanks.
Dad: Look, Bada! It's your favorite! Chocolate ice cream!
Bada: No, thank you. I want to eat it on the beach.
Mom: I have a great idea. Do you still want to go to the beach?
Hana: Yes, but it's raining, Mom. We'll get all wet!
Mom: But if you went swimming, you'll still get wet. Right?
Hana: There's no one on the beach, Mom.
Mom: That's what makes it special. We have the beach all to ourselves.
Bada: Can we go in the water?
Dad: Of course!
Hana: This is so much fun! Swimming in the rain is better than swimming in the sun! Oh, look! A rainbow! It’s beautiful!
It rained again the next day. But we still went to the beach. Dad said we should always look on the brighter side of things. Even if it rained, we still had lots of fun.

68.title: A Visit from Sunny and Tom

paragraphs.text: Guess what? Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom are coming to visit! Aunt Sunny says she has something very special to tell us! I wonder what it is.
Hana: When are Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom coming?
Mom: Next Saturday. They're going to stay with us.
Bada: Where will they sleep?
Mom: In Hana's room. So you have to sleep with your brothers, okay?
Hana: But Mom . . .
Dad: Hana. Aunt Sunny and Uncle Tom are our guests. We want them to feel welcome, right?
Hana: Yes, Dad . . .
Sunny: Hana, you've grown! We've missed you so much.
Hana: Me, too! I really enjoyed our trip to California last year.
Tom: Next time you come, you'll meet someone new.
Hana: New? What are you talking about? A new friend?
Sunny: We'll tell you later.
Bada: Hana! Read me this story!
Hana: No, Bada! I'm going to sleep. Go to your own bed.
Bada: But I'm not sleepy! Just this story, please?

Hana: I wish I was sleeping in my own bed. Oh, Bada is so loud! I can't sleep! Oh, no! There's somebody in the kitchen! Maybe it's a burglar. Should I wake Mom and Dad up? What about Bada and Hada? What if the burglar goes in there?
Sunny: Who's there? Hana?
Hana: Aunt Sunny! What are you doing here?
Sunny: Did I wake you? Sorry, Hana. I was so hungry.
Hana: Oh, maybe you didn't have enough for dinner.
Sunny: I had a lot for dinner. But I’m hungry again.
Hana: Oh, should I wake Mom up? She can make you pancakes.
Sunny: No, that's okay. I like sandwiches. Remember—Uncle Tom said next time you visit, you'll meet someone new.
Hana: Yes. Who is it? Do I know her?
Sunny: It may be a girl or a boy. I don't know.
Hana: You don't know who it is?
Sunny: Not yet. Hana, I'm going to have a baby.
Hana: A baby?
Sunny: Tom and I want a family of our own. We want children just like you, Bada, and Hada.
Hana: Wow! A baby.
Aunt Sunny is going to have a baby! I can't wait! She wants children just like us. She says we're special. I think so, too.

69.title: Chuseok, A Day to Give Thanks

paragraphs.text: This month we have Chuseok. It's a time to give thanks and remember our ancestors.
Mom: Hana! Grandma bought you a gift.
Hana: For me? But it's not my birthday.
Mom: I know. It's for Chuseok.
Bada: What about me, Mommy? Where's my present?
Mom: Here you are.
Hana: Oh, Mommy! It's so pretty!
Mom: It's lovely, Hana! You can wear that when we go to Grandma's house at Chuesok. Hana, can you help me carry this, please?
Hana: But what if it gets on my dress?
Mom: Don't be silly, Hana! Here, put this on. Then your dress won't get dirty.
Hana: It's dirty, Mom! My dress will get dirty too!
Mom: Hana! Chuseok is a day to give thanks. It's a day we help each other and show that we love each other. Now put this apron on!
Bada: Oops!
Hana: Oh, my dress! My dress! Look what you did, Bada!
Mom: It's okay. We'll find something else for you to wear.
Grandma: Here comes Hana. Come sit next to me, dear. Chuseok is a special day to give thanks. It doesn't matter how we look or what we eat, as long as we are together as a family.
Grandma is right. Sometimes we forget to be thankful. I learned a valuable lesson. It's not important what we have but what we give.
I love autumn! I love the blue skies. This year we are going to Mt. Sorak to see the colorful leaves on the trees!
Dad: What are you doing? We're leaving soon.
Bada: I don't want to go.
Hana: Can Bada and I stay here? We don't want to go hiking.
Mom: No, you can't. Besides, I know you'll love Mount Sorak. Now, come on!
Hana: Wow! Look at the beautiful colors! Why do leaves change colors?
Dad: Because the trees are getting ready for winter.
Mom: All leaves have green, yellow, and orange in them. But in the summer, the green color is the strongest.
Bada: Why?
Mom: Because of the sun, and water from the tree. But when the weather gets cooler, the tree gets less sun and water.
Dad: So the green fades, and the other colors like yellow and orange become brighter.
Bada: Here's a red one!
Mom: Yes! There are red and purple leaves too.
Dad: Hana, you like maple syrup on your pancakes, right?
Hana: Yummy! I love maple syrup.
Mom: Well, that syrup comes from the trees!
Hana: Wow! I never knew that!
Dad: Bada! Pick that up!
Mom: Never throw your garbage on the ground.
Bada: But why?
Dad: Do you throw garbage in your room? In your house?
Bada: No, only in the trash can.
Mom: Well, this is the trees' house. And it is home to the birds, squirrels, and other living things too. We mustn't make it dirty. Do you understand?
Bada: Yes, Mommy. Sorry, little squirrel!
Dad: Now, let's all take a picture.
Hana & Bada: CHEESE!
We spent three days in Mount Sorak. Mommy and Daddy taught us so much. We learned about trees, birds, and animals. I’m glad we didn't stay inside and watch TV.
Last night my grandma got very sick. Mommy and Daddy had to go to the hospital. So I had to stay with Bada at night.
Hana: Is Grandma going to be okay?
Mom: I hope so, Hana. Will you be okay looking after Bada?
Hana: Yes, don't worry, Mom. We'll be fine.
Dad: If anything happens, call me on my cell phone. Okay?
Mom: We'll be back soon.
Dad: Don't open the door for anyone!
Hana & Bada: We won't!
Bada: Hana! Someone is here!
Hana: Mommy and Daddy said not to open the door.
From outside the door: Hana! Bada! It’s Minji's mom.
Hana: Minji's mom?
Bada: Maybe it's not Minji's mom!
Minji's mom: Hana! Open the door! It’s cold out here!
Hana: It doesn't sound like Minji's mom.
Minji's mom: Hana! Bada! Open this door right now! Your mom called me! She wanted me to come over. Now, open up!
Hana: Do you believe her?
Bada: Let's call Dad!
Hana: Oh! He's not answering. Oh, no!
Bada: Hana. Let's call the police!
Hana: Hello? Is this the police? My name is Hana. There is someone outside my house. And my mommy and daddy aren't home.
Police: Hana? This is the police. Please open the door.
Hana: Oh! It really was you!
Mom: What happened! What's going on here! Is everything okay?
Minji's mom: Hana wouldn't open the door. I told her it was me!
Hana: But Daddy said not to open the door for anyone.
Dad: You did the right thing, Hana. It's my fault.
Hana: I’m really sorry.
Minji's mom: No, you did the right thing.
Mom: I should have called you, Hana, and said Minji's mom was coming. I’m sorry.
Bada: How is Grandma?
Dad: She's going to be okay.
What a night! I'm glad everything turned out fine. My dad said it's always better to be safe than sorry.
